- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to downward corrections.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >85), leading to overcorrection; cap forecast peaks at 5–10% below prior high.
- If sentiment shows strong mean-reversion signals (e.g., alternating +/– sentiment), model tends to lag in correcting mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early-term volatility; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
